_note: I045: corrections and stack-frame comments found while writing docs/code/cop-dispatch.md. Evidence: rg '^\s+BRK #' over extracted/ finds 289 instructions (HandleBrk said about a hundred); CopFillerTable_3D_7F has one #$0020 word (index $26); SpawnActorBefore links the new actor on the $3E side of the caller (I044: it runs right after the caller) but its part note still said earlier; Cop82/Cop83/Cop9E yield without writing $18 (the resume pointer comes from Cop80/Cop81/Cop9D) and SetActorAnimFrame puts the step duration in $14, so the next call is duration + 1 frames later, not next frame; CopExitJump writes only the PC word of the COP frame ($02,S), so a jump stays in the bank of the COP; no script uses a COP 81 repeat count below 2. Open points: questions/I045_questions.md.

edit.find: about a hundred call sites: sword swings, spawns, pickups, deaths, scripts
edit.with: 289 BRK #n instructions in extracted/: sword swings, spawns, pickups, deaths, scripts

edit.find: Clobbers: DP $3B-$3D; A and P restored (PHA/PLA, RTI).
edit.with: Clobbers: DP $3B-$3D; A and P restored (PHA/PLA, RTI). It never writes the script pointer $38-$3A, so a BRK between COP commands or inside a handler (Cop39_DamagePlayer) leaves the script alone.
Filler words (#$0000 and #$FFFF, plus one #$0020 at index $26, id $63)

22015.text: After PHA the frame is A (2 bytes), P, PC (BRK address + 2), PB: $04,S = PC, $06,S = the bank

22049.text: Native COP frame: $01,S = P, $02,S = PC (COP address + 2), $04,S = PB; this reads the bank of the script

edit.find: A wait command (Cop05, Cop82, Cop83, CopAD) does not move past itself while the wait lasts: it saves a resume pointer that re-runs the same COP next frame and yields.
edit.with: A wait command does not move past itself while the wait lasts: Cop05 and CopAD save a resume pointer that re-runs their own COP and yield; Cop82, Cop83 and Cop9E yield with the resume pointer that the animation command before them (Cop80, Cop81, Cop9D) saved, which points at the wait command in the usual pair.

edit.find: an actor linked before X runs earlier in the actor loop.
edit.with: it sits on the $3E side of X, so it runs right after X in the same frame (the actor loop follows $3E).

edit.find: Replaces the return address on the stack and returns with RTI.
edit.with: Replaces only the PC word of the COP frame (the bank byte stays, so a jump target is always in the bank of the COP) and returns with RTI, which also restores the P the script had at the COP.

edit.find: The script resumes next time from $18,X/$36,X.
edit.with: The actor loop calls the script again at $18,X/$36,X once the wait counter $14 has run out (a plain yield leaves it at 0, so the next frame).

25793.text: $02,S is the PC word of the COP frame; the bank at $04,S is not touched, so the script continues in its own bank

25801.text: Two 16-bit PLAs drop the 4-byte COP frame (P, PC, PB); RTL then returns to the address the scheduler pushed (StepActorMotion - 1)

edit.find: carry clear = a step was loaded, the actor yields and re-runs Cop82 next frame (the resume pointer points at it)
edit.with: carry clear = a step was loaded (its duration is now in $14), the actor yields and re-runs Cop82 when that wait has run out (the resume pointer points at it)
otherwise yield; the step duration is in $14, so the next call comes that many frames + 1 later.

edit.find: Out: counter zero: continues; otherwise yield while a step is running.
edit.with: Out: counter zero: continues; otherwise yield while a step is running. The counter is decremented before it is tested, so a count of 0 would run 65536 times; no script uses a COP 81 count below 2.
